precepts.text: Ye shall be hated of all nations for Christ's name's sake: they know Christ is in us and that Christ is black, so if they hate Christ they hate us, and our people are coming up missing and hung from trees because we are a hated people.
precepts.point: Because God chose us out of the world, the world hates us. Christ is telling us plainly that we are hated.

note.label: You Are Hated And In Hell

precepts.text: Every branch in me that beareth not fruit: you're not increasing in the fruits of the spirit. You're the same grimy person you was from five years back; there's no change in you, no transformation in you. It goes for men and women: you're the same gossiper, murmurer, complainer that you was five years ago; you're just here with a fringes and a border blue. He taketh away: take you away and kill you, that's what it's talking about. And every branch that beareth fruit, he purgeth it, that it may bring forth more fruit. You got to be purged to bring forth more fruit. There's things in us: I got to cut this off, cut that person off from you, cut this out of your soul, your spirit, so you can bear more fruit.
precepts.point: But those mine enemies, which would not that I should reign over them, bring hither, and slay them before me. Churches don't read that; churches will look at that and go, no, we're not reading that in Sunday school. You know what it means further? You ain't going to just be able to do what you want to do. You was put on this earth to do what the Most High and Christ said, and if you don't do that, then there's no reason for you to live. He said, if you don't want to do what you were created for, bring him before me and end his existence.

note.label: Living Your Life As A Hireling

precepts.why:
“Take from him the pound, and give it to him that hath ten pounds.” Imagine the order, like the king in Game of Thrones giving orders to the men next to the throne. It's pure order. “For I say unto you, That unto every one which hath shall be given; and from him that hath not, even that he hath shall be taken away from him.”

John shows the same judgment: “Every branch in me that beareth not fruit he taketh away.” Not bearing fruit means you're not increasing in the fruits of the spirit. You're the same grimy person you were five years back; there's no change in you, no transformation. It goes for men and women: the same gossiper, murmurer, complainer you were five years ago, just here with fringes and a border of blue. He taketh away means he takes you away and kills you.

“and every branch that beareth fruit, he purgeth it, that it may bring forth more fruit.” You've got to be purged to bring forth more fruit. There are things in us that have to be cut: cut this off, cut that person off from you, cut this out of your soul and your spirit, so you can bear more fruit.

We've seen it. Brothers came among us with certain skills and did not expand on them, so the Most High, like musical chairs, moved them out of the way. Other brothers came in, took that office and ran with it, and you don't hear anything about the men who were here with the ability to do just that.

precepts.text: I am the true vine, the root and offspring of David, Revelation 22:16, and my Father is the husbandman; ye are God's husbandry, 1 Corinthians 3:9. Every branch that beareth not fruit he taketh away, because one bad apple spoils the bunch and hinders growth; every branch that beareth fruit he purgeth that it may bring forth more. Abide in me, for the branch cannot bear fruit of itself.
precepts.point: The fear is not the fear of the servant who hid his talent or the brother making excuses because he is nervous; Psalms 119:120, my flesh trembleth for fear of thee and I am afraid of thy judgments. He is the King of terrors.

note.label: The Beauty And The Beast

precepts.why:
“By mercy and truth iniquity is purged.” Going into Passover season, which is also purging season, we refocus and get rid of the spiritual leaven known as sin. Christ shows how the purging is done: “I am the true vine, and my Father is the husbandman.”

A vine is nothing more than a root sprouting through the ground, and Christ is that root: “I am the root and the offspring of David, and the bright and morning star.” And the Father is the husbandman because we are what he planted: “ye are God’s husbandry, ye are God’s building.” We are his plants, his trees, which in that day become the trees of righteousness.

“Every branch in me that beareth not fruit he taketh away.” That is why we cannot be like the brother who had the talent and hid it. If we do not bring forth fruit, he takes away our candlestick: you did not do what I created you to do, so you cannot be here. One bad apple spoils the bunch, and you are going to hinder growth, so you have to be taken out of the way.

“and every branch that beareth fruit, he purgeth it, that it may bring forth more fruit. Now ye are clean through the word which I have spoken unto you.” That is the purging of Proverbs 16:6: iniquity purged, so we keep growing in the spirit and getting closer to our Lord and our God.

“Abide in me, and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, except it abide in the vine; no more can ye, except ye abide in me.” We have to stay steadfast and abide in Christ: not loving our pleasures or our lust more than Christ, but doing the will of the Father and his Son.

precepts.text: The branch that beareth not fruit he taketh away: unproductive, and he will kill you. The one that bears is purged, and the purging is the trials.
precepts.point: Out of thine own mouth will I judge thee, thou wicked servant. Men think they can be an Israelite and do nothing.

note.label: The Gospel Is Black Liberation

precepts.text: If ye keep my commandments, ye shall abide in my love; even as I have kept my Father's commandments; that is how Christ walked.
precepts.point: The blood was not eaten: the sin offering whose blood was brought into the tabernacle to reconcile was not eaten but burnt in the fire. Israel does not mess with the blood; Esau eats the blood, not us.

note.label: Leviticus 6: The Trespass Offering and the Fire That Shall Never Go Out

precepts.why:
This is how Christ walked: “If ye keep my commandments, ye shall abide in my love; even as I have kept my Father’s commandments, and abide in his love.”

He kept his Father’s commandments and abode in his love. That is the sinless walk that made him the most holy sin offering, and following his steps means keeping the commandments as he did.

precepts.text: Ye are clean through the word which Christ has spoken; the cleansing did not change in the New Testament.
precepts.point: We get clean by taking heed to the word and the commandments, not by water baptism.

note.label: Psalm 18: The Song of the Elect in the Last Days

precepts.why:
Christ tells his disciples, “Now ye are clean through the word which I have spoken unto you.” Ye are clean through the word, the same way a young man cleanses his way in Psalms 119:9.

The cleansing did not change in the New Testament. It was never water baptism; it is the word. David's clean hands, recompensed by the Lord, came from keeping the ways of the Lord and his statutes, and Christ says the same: clean through the word.

precepts.text: We are made clean through the word spoken to us; when we ask to be cleansed we must stand in Christ, abiding in the word to stay on the path of righteousness.
precepts.point: David asks to be washed thoroughly from his iniquity and cleansed from his sin. The question is: how are we going to be washed?

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

precepts.why:
Christ told his disciples, “Now ye are clean through the word which I have spoken unto you.” We are made clean through the word spoken to us. That lines up with Psalm 119: a young man cleanses his way by taking heed according to the word.

So when we ask, as David did, to be washed and cleansed, we must stand in Christ, abiding in the word, to stay on the path of righteousness. The word is what makes us clean.

precepts.text: Now ye are clean through the word which He has spoken; it is the word of the Most High that cleanses us from our sins.
precepts.point: I will meditate in Thy precepts. We have to meditate on the word of the Most High day and night, the same thing said in Joshua 1:8, delighting in His statutes and not forgetting His word.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:
“Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way? by taking heed thereto according to thy word.” Christ says the same: “Now ye are clean through the word which I have spoken unto you.”

It is the word of the Most High that cleanses us from our sins. It cleanses our brains, our mind, cleaning the filth that is within our heart, which is actually the mind. The word hidden in the heart is what keeps a man from sinning against him.

precepts.text: Ye are My friends if ye do whatsoever I command you, meaning follow this Bible.
precepts.point: I am a companion of all them that fear Thee, and of them that keep Thy precepts. You have to be a companion, a friend, to those that keep the laws of the Most High; that is who your companions need to be.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:
“I am a companion of all them that fear thee, and of them that keep thy precepts.” Christ says the same of friendship: “Ye are my friends, if ye do whatsoever I command you.”

Friendship with Christ is following this Bible, doing whatsoever he commands. So you have to be a companion, a friend, to those that keep the laws of the Most High; that is who your companions need to be.

precepts.text: "Now ye are clean through the word which I have spoken unto you," showing the cleansing comes through the word.
precepts.point: We cannot heal a body today, but we heal every day with the word: drug dealers, baby mothers, and survivors of mental, physical, alcoholic, drug, and religious abuse are healed when they receive the truth. When people say we do not feed the poor, the truth is the poor have the gospel preached to them, and that is the healing.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

precepts.why:
“Now ye are clean through the word which I have spoken unto you.” The cleansing comes through the word.

That is how we heal every day. Drug dealers, baby mothers, and survivors of mental, physical, alcoholic, drug and religious abuse are healed when they receive the truth. The man at the gate was made whole by the name of Jesus Christ; our people are made clean by his word.

precepts.text: Christ said, Now ye are clean through the word which I have spoken unto you; his baptism cleanses you consciously through his word, the laws and testimony.
precepts.point: Then the apostles laid their hands on them and they received the Holy Ghost, after they had repented and believed in Christ. There are two different baptisms: John's water baptism, which came from the Levitical purification laws and was symbolic of repentance, and Christ's baptism with the Holy Ghost, which is the laws and the cleansing of the conscience. Water can only wash the dirt off the skin; it cannot clean the evil in your mind. Christ magnified the law within the conscience, showing that sin starts in the mind, so his cleansing purifies your consciousness through his word.

note.label: Acts 8: The Word Scattered Abroad, and the Baptism unto the Conscience

precepts.why:
“Now ye are clean through the word which I have spoken unto you.” Christ's baptism cleanses you consciously through his word, the laws and testimony. That is the Holy Ghost they received when the apostles laid hands on them.

Christ magnified the law within the conscience, showing that sin starts in the mind. Water cannot clean the evil in your mind; his word can, so his cleansing purifies your consciousness.

precepts.text: Now ye are clean through the word which I have spoken unto you, cleansing the scattered nation by the word.
precepts.point: To "slay and eat" means to teach and cleanse the scattered Israelites through the word of God.

note.label: Acts 11: The Gentiles Are Scattered Israel

precepts.why:
“Now ye are clean through the word which I have spoken unto you.”

To “slay and eat” means to teach and cleanse the scattered Israelites through the word of God. The word is what makes them clean. Peter was sent to Cornelius to speak the word, and by it the unclean men of the sheet were cleansed.
